description: English Wikipedia pages for Crusades reference notes. Keep this list at battle, siege, or campaign-action scale rather than the whole Crusades umbrella.

pages.title: Crusades
pages.note: Broad context only. Use specific battle and siege pages for tactical extraction.

pages.title: Siege of Nicaea
pages.note: Early crusader-Byzantine cooperation, fortified city pressure, and negotiated control.

pages.title: Battle of Dorylaeum (1097)
pages.note: March column vulnerability, Turkish mounted archery, and relief by divided crusader forces.

pages.title: Siege of Antioch
pages.note: Long siege, famine, internal betrayal, counter-siege pressure, and morale crisis.

pages.title: Siege of Jerusalem (1099)
pages.note: Assault on a fortified holy city, siege engines, water scarcity, and final storming.

pages.title: Battle of Ascalon
pages.note: Rapid post-siege field battle, surprise, camp attack, and consolidation after Jerusalem.

pages.title: Siege of Edessa (1144)
pages.note: Fall of a frontier county, weak garrison coordination, and strategic shock.

pages.title: Battle of Montgisard
pages.note: Outnumbered Frankish strike, shock cavalry, surprise, and charismatic leadership.

pages.title: Battle of Hattin
pages.note: Water denial, heat, encirclement, missile pressure, and army collapse.

pages.title: Siege of Acre (1189–1191)
pages.note: Long coastal siege, naval supply, disease, coalition politics, and counter-siege.

pages.title: Battle of Arsuf
pages.note: March discipline, harassment by mounted forces, controlled cavalry countercharge.

pages.title: Sack of Constantinople
pages.note: Diversion of campaign objective, assault on a major city, naval access, and alliance breakdown.
